title: Add modular RAG authoring CLI and typed tool-stub generator
author: Aisha Patel
release_notes: Introduce a local-first RAG authoring CLI that scaffolds modular templates and generates typed tool stubs for TS/Python; includes minimal telemetry probes and a smoke test harness.
description: Motivation: Authoring RAG applications often requires gluing scaffolding, tool stubs, and telemetry probes together. This PR adds a lightweight, local-first authoring CLI (rag-author) to help developers scaffold modular RAG templates, generate typed tool stubs for TypeScript and Python, and wire in small telemetry probes for live-step tracing. The intent is to reduce onboarding friction for engineers experimenting with RAG patterns while keeping artifacts small and opinionated for production readiness. What this PR delivers: 1) rag-author CLI (node) with commands: init (create project from modular templates), add-tool (generate typed tool stub for ts|py), dev (run a local shim runtime with live reload), smoke (run a minimal end-to-end simulation using saved prompts), and telemetry-on (inject lightweight probes). 2) Three modular template blueprints: minimal-microservice, browser-embedded, and batch-indexer. 3) Typed tool-stub generator that emits TypeScript interfaces + runtime adapter and a Python async shim with typed dataclasses. 4) Compact telemetry probes (opt-in) that emit structured events to local file or stdout and include a step-id for later correlation with eval harnesses. 5) Basic docs and quickstart guide: examples/README.md and CLI man page. Checklist: - [x] scaffolding and templates implemented - [x] tool-stub generator for TS + Python - [x] local shim runtime with sample indexer and memory-backed KV - [x] telemetry probes (file/console) - [x] smoke test harness + CI job - [x] docs/quickstart written Non-goals: this is not a production runtime; no heavy integrations (no DB/Kafka) and no opinionated deployment flows. Usage (short): - npx rag-author init my-rag-app --template minimal-microservice - cd my-rag-app && npx rag-author add-tool 'search_client' --lang ts - Start local dev runtime: npx rag-author dev - Run smoke tests: npx rag-author smoke Why unique: unlike existing quickstarts this PR focuses on the authoring loop and strong typed stubs to accelerate tool-calling integrations in both TypeScript and Python while keeping the templates intentionally minimal to be used as building blocks for platform and product teams. Commits (high-level): - feat(cli): initial rag-author scaffolding and command parser - feat(templates): add minimal-microservice, browser-embedded, batch-indexer blueprints - feat(generator): typed tool-stub generator for ts and py - feat(dev): local shim runtime and live reload - feat(telemetry): opt-in probes + step correlation - test(ci): add smoke test and CI job - docs: quickstart and examples/README.md Files changed (high level): - cli/bin/rag-author.js - templates/minimal-microservice/{template files} - templates/browser-embedded/{template files} - templates/batch-indexer/{template files} - generator/ts-stub-template.ts - generator/py_stub_template.py - examples/README.md - ci/smoke-rag-author.yml Review conversation summary: "Tomás: requested clearer failure modes for add-tool when type signatures are unknown; suggested adding validation for reserved tool names. Claire: asked to make telemetry opt-in by default and to add a small sample of a step trace in the README. Michael: requested an expanded smoke test to cover the dev shim and a failure-case test. Author replies: clarified that telemetry is opt-in by default and added docs; improved add-tool validation to reject reserved names and added a lenient fallback; extended smoke test to assert step-id propagation. CI: initial run failed due to flaky playground env in smoke job; re-ran after making the local shim deterministic (seeded random) and CI passed. Merge: squash-merged into main on 2026-02-20. Related work: ENG-7342 (authoring ergonomics), PM-198 (quickstart roadmap), SUP-1123 (support case: customers need fast tool-stub onboarding). Backwards-incompatible changes: none. Follow-ups: - add optional connectors (Postgres/S3) in a later PR - add plugin hooks for telemetry exporters - produce a GitHub template repository from the minimal blueprint
